newsitem.title: GERMANY: German 1996 grain crop estimate raised to 42 mln T.
newsitem.headline: German 1996 grain crop estimate raised to 42 mln T.

text.p: The German 1996 grain harvest was now estimated at 42 million tonnes, rounded, up 5.3 percent from last year and compared with 41 million expected for 1996 in an Aug 29 estimate, the agriculture ministry said.
Western German crops were put at 28.8 million (26.0 million last year) and eastern Germany's at 13.2 (13.8).
Average yields rose by 2.5 percent to 6.26 tonnes per hectare (tph) versus 6.11 tph last year.
The area was expanded by 2.7 percent over 1995 to 6.71 million hectares.
The ministry said the average quality was broadly similar to last year but wheat and rye in some regions suffered quality losses because of cool and rainy weather during harvesting.
This meant some wheat and rye designated for bread making did not qualify for this purpose.
But malting barley qualities were nearly all very good.
The ministry gave the following breakdown -- wheat 18.9 million tonnes (17.8 million 1995), winter barley 7.9 (9.0), spring barley 4.1 (2.8), rye 4.2 (4.5), triticale 2.1 (1.6) and oats 1.6 (1.4).
The remainder of the total was mixed grain and maize.
Yields in the individual grains were as follows -- Winter barley declined by 10.2 percent to 5.61 tph and rye by 1.5 percent to 5.17 tph.
But winter wheat yields rose 5.8 percent to 7.32, triticale's by 2.5 percent to 5.83 and other spring grain yields were also higher.
